top_story: Gaza’s residents remain trapped in a prolonged condition of ruin, disease, and hunger that has turned survival into the organizing fact of daily life, underscoring how the region’s wars continue to erode civilian resilience long after headline battles fade. A separate but related escalation has widened that civilian toll beyond the Levant: the early-war U.S. strike on a school in Minab, Iran, left a lasting symbol of how quickly state confrontation can translate into mass harm for families and first responders. The most recent Houthi strikes on Saudi airports, which killed at least three people and wounded dozens, show that cross-border attacks are now pressuring Gulf infrastructure and exposing the limits of deterrence even as outside powers move more troops and equipment into the theater. The regional picture is one of conflict systems feeding each other, with civilian spaces increasingly absorbing the consequences of military signaling and strategic expansion.
